title: The City of Refuge
focus: Harlem as promised refuge and trap

teacherSummary.text: King Solomon Gillis flees North Carolina after shooting a white man and arrives in Harlem, amazed to see a Black policeman. He trusts Mouse Uggam, a fellow Southerner, who uses him to sell drugs. When the police come for him, Gillis fights, then sees the Black officer, and gives himself up with something exultant in his face.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Cullud policemans” slowly and put it in my own words: Fresh from North Carolina, Gillis is amazed to see a Black policeman giving orders to white drivers. Next, craft. I notice the dialect and the plural "policemans," which show his excitement. The strongest word is “policemans”: his grammar shows his rural voice and the newness of what he sees. Then, effect. Why is Gillis so astonished? My answer: Gillis is so astonished because he sees a Black policeman directing white drivers; for Gillis that authority means Harlem is a place of freedom, a hope the story will test.
